data.name: Eduard
data.gender_notes: Eduard is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name 'Edward', meaning 'wealthy guardian' or 'rich in grace'. In Christian tradition, Eduard is associated with St. Edward the Confessor, the last Anglo-Saxon king of England before the Norman Conquest. The name Eduard carries the meaning “Rich in Grace” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Eduard usually hope their child will grow to embody rich in grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name with deep religious roots, symbolizing the grace and protection of God.
data.etymology: Eduard belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rich in Grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eduard total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_latin.name: Eduardus
in_latin.meaning: Nomen masculinum ex Germanico et Gothico derivatum, significans fortis et prosperus
in_latin.long_meaning: Eduardus est nomen masculinum, quod a Germanico et Gothico derivatum est. Insignificat fortitudo et prosperitatem. Ex origine, Eduardus erat nomen regum Anglorum, qui a 9o saeculo usque ad 11um saeculum regnaverunt. In historia Christiana, Eduardus fuit nomen sancti, qui in Ecclesia Catholica et Ecclesia Anglicana veneratur.

in_english.name: Eduard
in_english.meaning: Strong and prosperous name derived from Germanic and Gothic roots
in_english.long_meaning: The name Eduard is derived from the Germanic and Gothic roots, signifying strength and prosperity. In Christian tradition, Eduard was the name of a saint who was venerated in the Catholic and Anglican churches. The name is associated with qualities such as courage, resilience, and success. In modern times, Eduard is used as a given name across various Christian cultures, symbolizing a strong and prosperous individual.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eduard reached its peak popularity in the 19th and early 20th centuries, particularly in Europe and the United States. It is a name that connotes a sense of wealth, protection, and wisdom. In some cultures, it is also believed that the name Eduard carries a sense of nobility and strength.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Eduard holds a deeper spiritual meaning. It is a reminder of the rich grace and blessings that God bestows upon us, making us His guardians and stewards of His creation. It is also a reminder of St. Edward the Confessor, who stood firm in his faith amid the political upheaval of his time and is remembered as a model of faithfulness and unwavering commitment to God. Therefore, Eduard is a name that inspires us to be rich in grace, firm in our faith, and good stewards of God's blessings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eduard, derived from Edo or Eudes, means "wealth, riches, prosperity" in Germanic origin. Symbolically, it represents the pursuit of spiritual and material abundance in one's life, embodying the values of hard work, determination, and faith.

historical_references.reference: Eduard I, The Confessor, was the Duke of Swabia from 1245 to 1268 and was the founder of the Swabian Anonymous Brotherhood, a charitable organization. He was also a Wittelsbach prince, the second son of Duke Otto I of Swabia and Agnes of Hohenstaufen.

Eduard I, The Black Prince, was the eldest son of King Edward III of England and Queen Philippa of Hainault. He became the Prince of Wales and largely ruled the country during his father's campaigns in France. He was also known as 'The Black Prince' due to his participation in the Battle of Poitiers, where he defeated the French army and captured their king, Jean II.
historical_references.context: Late Middle Ages, England and France
